messages:
alex b: Heads-up — we're planning to unpin the old default model next week. quick q: do we want an SDK 'shim' that rewrites requests from clients that don't send the new X-Model-Version header?

maria s: Good question. product prefers explicit headers, but we also care about smooth rollouts for customers. what's the risk vector for silently rewriting?

david k: Risk: clients depending on previous default behaviour might see quality/cost/regressions. Shim helps backward compat for a short window, but it hides the change and delays client upgrades.

alex b: Right. My proposal: ship a 2-week shim in SDKs that maps missing header -> previous pinned model, and log telemetry + emit a deprecation warning response header. After 2 weeks, SDK removes shim.

jen r: From docs POV we need: deprecation notice page, SDK changelog entry, and example curl snippets showing the X-Model-Version header. Also ensure migration guide for dedicated/private users.

maria s: Is the deprecation warning going into the HTTP response or as part of an admin email? We should do both. Response header is immediate and machine-readable. Email + console banner for customers with lots of usage.

david k: Implementation notes: add middleware in the platform router that: 1) if header missing and sdk-Client-Version header present -> rewrite to pinned model and set X-Deprecation-Warning: "model-default-deprecated"; 2) emit metric shim_rewrite{client_sdk, org}.

alex b: Example header behavior:

```
# client without header -> server response
Request: POST /v1/generate
Headers:
  Authorization: Bearer x...
  Content-Type: application/json
(no X-Model-Version)

Response: 200 OK
Headers:
  X-Model-Version: redwood-opus-v1  # server chose fallback
  X-Deprecation-Warning: default-model-unpinned; upgrade-to: X-Model-Version
```

jen r: Can we keep the exact header names stable? docs already reference X-Model-Version in a few places. Also add an audit log entry for rewrite events.

maria s: Timeline question: if we enable shim next Tue, when do we send emails and console banners?

david k: Suggested timeline:
- Today: final PR for middleware + metric logging
- Tomorrow: SDK PRs with opt-in shim behind a feature flag (npm alpha)
- Tue: enable server-side shim + start emitting metrics + enable response header warnings
- Wed: console banner + in-app notice for orgs > 10k tokens/day
- Next Mon (2 weeks): remove server-side shim, leave deprecation page and SDK warnings

alex b: Sounds good. One more: what about third-party integrations (Zapier/webhooks) that might not parse headers? We should also put a 1-minute payload-level notice in response body for those. Keep it compact.

jen r: I'll draft the deprecation page and include copy for email and console. Will tag examples for curl, python, node.

release-bot: Deployment scheduled: eng-platform/middleware/shim-mapping to canary at 2026-03-20T09:00Z. CI: green.

alex b: Thanks @release-bot. Anyone object to the 2-week window?

maria s: No objections from product. Agree keep it short.

david k: Dev concern: ensure rollback toggle exists (feature flag) and we can backfill telemetry for any spike. I'll add a kill-switch endpoint.

jen r: Docs draft link: https://redwood.internal/docs/drafts/default-model-deprecation (will post PR once reviewed).

alex b: Action items:
- david k: PR for middleware + metrics + kill-switch (due EOD today)
- jen r: deprecation page + examples (PR by EOD tomorrow)
- maria s: prepare email + console copy (send to growth/legal for sign-off)
- alex b: coordinate SDK PRs and publish alpha shim toggles

maria s: I'll create a short playbook for support to follow if customers report regressions.

alex b: Great. Let's sync async — ping this thread when PRs are up. :thumbsup:

docs-bot: New draft created: /drafts/default-model-deprecation-md (editable).

alex b: closing loop — thanks everyone.
